transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Sonia Patel (BluePeak CTO), Liam Carter (BluePeak ML Eng), Grace Nguyen (BluePeak Security)

Summary (auto): BluePeak currently uses OpenAI for most traffic and runs vLLM/TGI on-prem for latency sensitive batch jobs. They're evaluating Redwood Dedicated for predictable cost and data isolation. Main asks: how straightforward is model compatibility, can we reproduce evals, what does dedicated pricing look like, and what security controls are available.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm ava from redwood, and with me is marco ruiz our se. how's everyone doing?
[00:05] Sonia Patel: good thanks, yeah excited to talk. i'm sonia, cto at bluepeak. we run most stuff on open-ai's endpoints but have some local infra for latency.
[00:10] Marco Ruiz: great, quick agenda - understand current stack, pain points, desired sla/cost targets, and then go through migration compatibility and a benchmarking plan. sound good?
[00:15] Liam Carter: yep that works. i'll try to nerd out on performance bits.
[00:20] Grace Nguyen: and i'll be listening for security controls and audit stuff.

[02:00] Sonia Patel: to start, our infra - about 2.5M requests/month, mix of chat completions and embeddings. majority on OpenAI GPT-4 style models, and for high-throughput low-latency we spin up vLLM/TGI locally on a few nodes. cost is creeping up and we've hit rate-limiting occasionally.
[02:30] Marco Ruiz: makes sense. are you using function calling or structured outputs much?
[02:35] Liam Carter: yep function calls for enrichment, also heavy use of embeddings for search - around 500k embeddings a month.
[03:00] Ava Chen: when you say vLLM/TGI locally, that's for short-context real-time stuff or batching?
[03:10] Liam Carter: mostly batching for lower latency than OpenAI sometimes; we also keep a KV cache to avoid regen for repeated prefixes. it's a mix.

[05:00] Marco Ruiz: ok, main migration questions we usually see: 1) api compatibility - can you swap endpoints and preserve prompts? 2) eval parity - do responses match the quality of OpenAI? 3) infra & ops - how to size dedicated capacity and cost tradeoffs.
[05:30] Sonia Patel: exactly. on parity - we ran some internal evals and saw subtle differences when we moved models between providers; our ops folks worry about regressions.
[06:00] Marco Ruiz: totally. our onboarding approach is to run a mirrored eval harness - you give prompt sets, we'll run them on Redwood Dedicated with the same model family or closest equivalent and produce regression reports. we also support custom model artifacts if you have them.
[06:30] Grace Nguyen: when you say custom artifacts, do you mean we can bring our finetuned checkpoints? what's the k m s / key management story for that?
[06:40] Marco Ruiz: good q - on Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS integration (bring-your-key) for model artifacts and data at rest. for Private deployments we can do on-prem or VPC with HSM support if needed.

[08:15] Liam Carter: compatibility - tokenization differences have bitten us before. how do you handle byte-pair tokenization parity?
[08:25] Ava Chen: we maintain model mapping and tokenization libs; for most open models we bundle the appropriate tokenizer, but we always recommend running your prompt set as part of the benchmark to catch issues. sometimes BPE quirks show up (especially with new finetunes).

[10:00] Sonia Patel: what about throughput and latency? currently our p95 latency for chat is ~250ms using vLLM local nodes; OpenAI average is ~400ms for production traffic. we want to keep p95 under 300ms ideally.
[10:20] Marco Ruiz: on Dedicated we typically size pools to meet throughput SLOs - continuous batching and KV cache reduce per-token time. with a 4-GPU pool (A100 equiv) we expect to meet your 300ms p95 on models in the 7-13B family for short contexts; larger models need more tuning/quantization.
[10:50] Liam Carter: you mentioned quantization - do you do 4-bit q or int8? what's impact on quality?
[11:00] Marco Ruiz: we support multiple quantization profiles. int8/4-bit with tuned kernels - typically 4-bit (QLoRA-style) gives great perf with minimal quality drop for most prompts; part of the benchmark is quality vs quantized model.

[13:00] Grace Nguyen: security/regulatory wise - we need SOC 2 compliance, SAML SSO, per-token audit logs, and retention controls. also data residency for EU users.
[13:20] Ava Chen: Redwood Dedicated customers get enterprise controls - SOC 2 reports, SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC, audit logs, and per-customer retention policies. region pinning for data residency is supported on Dedicated and Private. we'll attach the security pack after the call.
[13:50] Sonia Patel: great. does Dedicated isolate customer data from other tenants?
[13:55] Marco Ruiz: yes, Dedicated is physically isolated GPU pools for your account; Private is the next step (VPC/on-prem) if you need complete control of the control plane.

[16:00] Liam Carter: one practical question: our pipelines call OpenAI's ChatCompletion APIs with function calling; how much change will we need in client code to hit Redwood?
[16:15] Ava Chen: minimal - Redwood's API is designed to be compatible with common patterns: chat/completions, function calling, embeddings. there are small differences in model names, but in most cases it's a drop-in with a config change. we'll provide compatibility notes.

[18:00] Sonia Patel: pricing - are we looking at pay-as-you-go or reserved capacity? our spend is high enough that committed makes sense.
[18:10] Ava Chen: we offer both - hosted usage billing and Dedicated reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits. Dedicated pricing includes base capacity, optional burst, and support tiers. i'll send you a committed capacity example showing unit economics vs OpenAI.

[20:00] Marco Ruiz: for the benchmark we'd like to run: 1) mirror 2k representative prompts across chat and function calling, 2) run embeddings batches, 3) measure latency P50/P95, cost per 1k tokens, and output diffs for eval parity. we can run multiple config variants (quantized, different batch sizes).
[20:30] Liam Carter: sounds good. we currently log exact tokens used per prompt so we can compare cost numbers. also, we'd like to test fallback: if Dedicated hits capacity, can requests go to Redwood hosted or another model?
[20:45] Marco Ruiz: yes, smart routing/fallback is supported - you can set policies to route to hosted or a smaller model variant under overload. it's configurable in the console.

[23:00] Grace Nguyen: about audit logs - how long do you retain by default and can we enforce shorter/longer retention?
[23:10] Ava Chen: defaults are industry standard, but Dedicated customers can configure retention windows and export logs to your SIEM; we also provide token-level cost and latency traces per request.

[25:00] Sonia Patel: on bringing models - we sometimes run TGI racks for community models; can we bring our TGI artifacts into Dedicated?
[25:20] Marco Ruiz: yes, if you have compliant model artifacts we can take them. minor packaging steps may be needed - we'll give a runbook. for models that depend on a specific vLLM/TGI kernel we may need to validate or recompile kernels.

[27:00] Liam Carter: any limits on custom model size? we have a fine-tuned 16B we care about.
[27:10] Marco Ruiz: Dedicated supports up to 70B depending on GPU type; larger models need different cluster shapes. for 16B you're well within typical configs.

[29:00] Sonia Patel: what's the expected time to provision a Dedicated pool for benchmarking?
[29:10] Ava Chen: if we have contract terms in place provisioning can be hours; for a benchmark we can usually provision a temporary cluster in 2-3 business days. marco will own the provisioning for your benchmark.

[31:00] Marco Ruiz: operational notes - we'll run the bench with identical seeds where possible; we also capture hallucination/regression metrics via your eval harness. please expect some small deltas when moving between model families.
[31:30] Liam Carter: fair. also how do you handle KV cache warmup? we have high hit rates on prefixes during peak hours.
[31:40] Marco Ruiz: we have automatic prefix/KV caching and persistent KV cache options in Dedicated to keep warm caches across requests, reducing token compute. we'll show hit rate improvements in the benchmark report.

[34:00] Grace Nguyen: legal/procurement - we have a standard DPA and a security questionnaire. who should we send those to?
[34:10] Ava Chen: send the DPA and questionnaire to contracts@redwood.com; i'll also put you in touch with our legal lead. we'll aim to return the security questionnaire within 3-5 business days.

[36:00] Sonia Patel: ok let's recap next steps.
[36:05] Ava Chen: recap - i'll send pricing and security pack, marco will provision the benchmark cluster and share scripts, sonia will share a representative prompt set and eval metrics, grace to send the security questionnaire. we'll aim to start the benchmark by 2026-12-29 and have an initial report within 2 weeks of run completion.
[36:30] Liam Carter: yep, that timeline works on our side.
[36:45] Marco Ruiz: one last thing - do you have any regulatory constraints for model hosting in the EU?
[36:50] Grace Nguyen: yes EU customer data must stay in eu regions; we can specify region pinning.
[37:00] Marco Ruiz: noted, we'll provision EU region resources for the benchmark where applicable.

[38:30] Sonia Patel: thanks all, that was useful. we'll follow up with the assets.
[38:40] Ava Chen: thanks everyone, appreciate it. we'll send the pack and calendar invites.

[40:00] (call ends)
